thesis: The AI supercycle is real and measurable — industry revenue tracking toward $1.29T in 2026 (+53%) on ~$600B of hyperscaler capex — but after a ~90% YTD run in the SOXX the entry demands selectivity: own the compute monopolist (NVDA) and sold-out HBM memory (MU), respect the digestion risk.

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
**OVERWEIGHT (selective)** over 12 months. Semiconductors are in a structural, AI-led expansion: IDC forecasts the global market surging past $1 trillion to ~$1.29T in 2026 (+52.8%), driven by AI infrastructure, a memory supercycle, and hyperscaler capex approaching ~$600B (+70% YoY). The bottlenecks have moved downstream — HBM and advanced packaging (CoWoS-class), then power and copper — which concentrates pricing power in the few names that control those choke points. After a ~90% YTD run in the sector ETFs, we are buyers of the choke-point owners (NVDA in compute, MU in memory) rather than the group indiscriminately. Sector sleeve 6–10%, single names 1–4%.

## MACRO & SECTOR BACKDROP
**Market size**: IDC projects 2026 semiconductor revenue of $1.29T (+52.8% YoY), with data-center semiconductor revenue alone reaching $477.1B. The industry crossed the ~$1T annual run-rate in early 2026.

**Capex engine**: Hyperscale capex crossed $100B per quarter for the first time in Q3 2025; the big four are expected to lift 2026 capex ~70% YoY to roughly $600B. DRAM capex is set to rise 14% to ~$61B and NAND capex 5% to ~$21B.

**Memory supercycle**: Suppliers are prioritizing HBM for AI servers, tightening conventional DRAM supply and pushing prices up across the complex. BofA estimates the 2026 HBM market at $54.6B, +58% YoY.

**The real constraints**: HBM availability and advanced packaging throughput (2.5D/3D integration, interposers, high-end substrates) now cap AI accelerator shipments — the backend has become a first-order growth limiter. Beyond silicon: electricity, copper (~27 tons per MW of data-center capacity; copper ~$5.61/lb after a record ~$6 in January 2026) and critical gases are rationing buildout speed.

**Geopolitics**: China data-center revenue is minimal across leading vendors due to export controls, with no recovery embedded in guidance (NVIDIA shipped zero H20 units last quarter and excludes China DC compute from guidance) — a free option if policy eases, not a risk to estimates.

## SUB-SECTOR DYNAMICS
**AI compute (NVDA, AMD, AVGO)**: NVIDIA printed $81.6B revenue in the April 2026 quarter (+85% YoY; data center $75.2B, +92%) and guided ~$91B. Custom-silicon (AVGO) and challenger (AMD) narratives are strong but the economics still pool at the platform leader.

**Memory (MU, SK hynix, Samsung)**: The tightest market in the complex. Micron's May-quarter revenue rose ~300% YoY to $41.5B and its HBM supply is effectively sold out on ~$100B of binding multi-year AI memory contracts.

**Equipment & foundry (AMAT, TSM)**: Beneficiaries of every path through the cycle; TSM monopolizes leading-edge logic, AMAT rides both logic and the 14%/5% DRAM/NAND capex lift.

**Performance check**: SOXX +91.7% YTD and PSI +103.6% YTD vs the S&P 500 — the crowd has arrived; forward returns now depend on earnings delivery, not re-rating.

## VALUATION
The sector trades on whether 2027 hyperscaler capex grows or digests. Street models still show upside at the leaders despite the run: NVDA consensus $301.62 (+43% vs $210.57), MU consensus $1,264–1,486 (vs $1,145). That embedded upside reflects earnings growth, not multiple expansion — NVDA trades at a market-relative discount to its own growth rate. The group's risk is a 2027 capex pause, which history says produces 30–50% drawdowns in the cyclicals (memory first).

## RISK ASSESSMENT
**Cycle risk**: AI capex digestion in 2027 is the bear case that matters; watch hyperscaler capex guidance revisions and HBM contract pricing.
**Concentration risk**: A handful of buyers (the big four hyperscalers) fund the entire cycle.
**Geopolitical risk**: Taiwan concentration in leading-edge logic; export-control escalation; tariff policy.
**Physical risk**: Power, copper, and packaging capacity can cap growth regardless of demand.
**Positioning risk**: After +90% YTD, entries should be staged; size the sleeve 6–10% with names 1–4%.
